checks.assessment: UserRole.self is bound to User.id and receives base read only; update is granted in the named disable_user operation exception. The User lifecycle transition guards active-to-disabled and writes status/disabled_at only. DELETE /users/{user_id} requires fresh auth.

checks.area: Cross-user disable concealment and retained children
checks.assessment: A foreign target yields 404 user_not_found and remains active on both adapters. Self-disable returns 204, later authorization/refresh fails closed, and the existing Todo row remains. The User transition itself has no Todo write or cascade path.

checks.area: Todo owner delete scope and guarded soft-delete
checks.assessment: TodoRole.owner is bound to immutable owner_id and retains delete permission. The delete transition uses deleted_at == none as its from-guard and changes only deleted_at; compiler lowering maps the delete transition to logical delete authorization while issuing a guarded UPDATE. Foreign deletion is concealed on SQLite.

GET, PATCH, list and repeat DELETE conceal a deleted Todo; tests verify 404s, list exclusion and that the row/title/status remain. CreateTodo and PatchTodo omit deleted_at, Delete has no body, and lifecycle mutation is through the transition. The migrated package declares retention but has no authored job or purge action; scheduling remains outside RM-106.

nonBlockingEvidenceNotes: The combined self-disable route test soft-deletes its only created Todo before disabling the User, so its row-exists assertion does not separately demonstrate that an active child retains deleted_at = null. The User transition is source-limited to User status/disabled_at, with no Todo cascade path.

Soft-delete runtime assertions compare title/status and the retained row, but do not set non-null due_at/reminder_sent_at values before deletion. The transition source changes deleted_at only; generated updated_at is expected to track that lifecycle change.
